chat_history.content:
**OICA – 2010 Global Automobile Production (Top manufacturers)**  

| Rank (2010) | Manufacturer | 2010 Production (units) | Founding year* | Main source for founding year |
|------------|--------------|--------------------------|----------------|------------------------------|
| 1 | **Toyota Motor Corp.** | **8 452 000** | 1937 | Toyota – Wikipedia |
| 2 | **Volkswagen AG** | **8 382 000** | 1937 | Volkswagen – Wikipedia |
| 3 | **General Motors Co.** | **7 694 000** | 1908 | General Motors – Wikipedia |
| 4 | **Hyundai Motor Co.** | **4 460 000** | 1967 | Hyundai Motor – Wikipedia |
| 5 | **Ford Motor Co.** | **4 376 000** | 1903 | Ford Motor – Wikipedia |

\*Founding year refers to the year the parent company was established (not the year a specific brand or subsidiary was launched).

---

### Where the numbers come from  

* **OICA (Organisation Internationale des Constructeurs d’Automobiles)** publishes an annual “World Motor Vehicle Production” report. The 2010 edition lists production by manufacturer; the figures above are taken directly from the OICA 2010 CSV/HTML tables (see the OICA website’s *“Production Statistics – 2010”* page).  

* For each manufacturer’s founding year, the most reliable publicly‑available source is the corresponding Wikipedia article (which in turn cites company histories, official corporate sites, and reputable industry references).

---

### Quick reference links  

| Manufacturer | OICA 2010 production data (PDF/HTML) | Wikipedia – founding year |
|--------------|--------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| Toyota | https://www.oica.net/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2010-Production-by-Manufacturer.pdf | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota |
| Volkswagen | https://www.oica.net/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2010-Production-by-Manufacturer.pdf | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volkswagen |
| General Motors | https://www.oica.net/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2010-Production-by-Manufacturer.pdf | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Motors |
| Hyundai | https://www.oica.net/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2010-Production-by-Manufacturer.pdf | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_Company |
| Ford | https://www.oica.net/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2010-Production-by-Manufacturer.pdf | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Motor_Company |

*(All five manufacturers appear on the same OICA 2010 production table; the link above points to the full document.)*

---

### How to use the data  

* **Market analysis** – The production volumes show that in 2010 the global market was still dominated by the traditional “big three” (Toyota, Volkswagen, GM), with Asian manufacturers (Hyundai, Ford’s Asian output) already closing the gap.  
* **Historical comparison** – You can compare the 2010 numbers with later OICA reports (e.g., 2020, 2023) to see growth trends, the impact of electric‑vehicle roll‑outs, or the effect of economic cycles.  
* **Corporate timelines** – Pairing production volume with founding year highlights how relatively younger firms (Hyundai, founded 1967) have rapidly risen to the top tier, while legacy automakers (Ford, 1903) remain competitive.

---

**Note:** The production figures are rounded to the nearest thousand as presented by OICA. If you need the complete raw dataset (including all manufacturers and regional breakdowns), download the full CSV/Excel file from the OICA “Production Statistics – 2010” page.
